title: ÆTHER: Zero Hour (modern action blockbuster main theme)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: A huge modern blockbuster film score, the main title theme of a big-screen action thriller set in today's Mumbai: a cyber attack blacks out the city at midnight and one agent races the clock to switch it back on. Cinematic, epic and hyped from the first second to the last: full symphony orchestra with powerful brass and fast driving strings, a big male choir chanting wordless syllables, massive hybrid cinematic drums and deep synth bass, a gritty electronic synth lead. Written the way today's biggest South Indian film composers score a mass action sequence: a raga melody, swinging half-time mass bounce, stop-and-slam full-band hits, choir answering the hook, the hook coming back bigger each time. Not DJ music, not EDM, not a club or concert track: it is film music. Raga Shanmukhapriya in E: E F# G A# B C D. The hook hammers B C D E in tight unison stabs, then falls E D C B A# G F# E, with gamakam bends on G and C. ONE memorable 5-note hook, B C D E C, runs through the whole track, passed between instruments. One steady tempo, 104 BPM half-time feel, never stopping. Real instruments named as themselves are played by real musicians, close, natural and dry, no heavy echo: thavil, solo violin, bansuri flute. Quiet electronic layer: chopped glitching veena stutters, pitched-down mridangam hits, reversed veena swells into each section. 0-3 s: one enormous low boom with a full brass blast, then a gritty bent synth plays a 3-note call E G B with the last note bent up. 3-14 s: a ticking clock pulse, deep synth bass, low male choir hum, fast pumping strings, tension at once, already loud. 14-26 s: hybrid drums and a real thavil crash in on the mass bounce; the hook on synth lead and brass together. 26-38 s: the hook passes to a fiery solo violin with slides, driving strings, choir shouts HEY on the accents. 38-50 s: bigger: brass and choir carry the hook, the drums double up; one beat of total silence, then a full-band slam. 50-64 s: a bansuri plays the hook in fast runs, answered by the synth lead; rising tension, taiko-style tom rolls. 64-80 s: the hook returns a whole step higher in F#, full orchestra, choir and drums, the biggest and most triumphant moment. 80-90 s: a korvai ending, three rising full-band hits, a final boom, then the 3-note call on solo brass. Loud and big from the very start, no soft intro, no slow or quiet middle, no lull longer than one beat, no gaps, no fade-out, no side-chain pumping, no white-noise risers, no drop-and-build EDM structure, no lyrics.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 11:30 on Midnight City: 'initial and mid part both are really boring... we need that hype, it's a cinematic world... not for DJ or concert, it's for the cinematic world, so think big.' Modern concept kept (11:21). Hype from second 0 (rule 9.13), hook every ~12 s (9.11), orchestra + choir + hybrid drums with electronic lead and Carnatic instruments as 2nd/3rd layer. Shanmukhapriya in E so the E G B logo call sits in the raga. Prompt mode, music_v2, one continuous generation.

story: A cyber attack blacks out today's Mumbai at midnight; one young agent races the clock across rooftops and highways to switch the city back on.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
